about: The narrated tour recorded by tools/record_tour.py. Each segment is one page; each beat is what is said while the page scrolls to 'to' (the first words of a heading a viewer can read). Record in daylight, when the solar and battery flows are moving.

beats.say: This is the hub, the page that lives on the wall tablet. It answers one question first: is the house all right?
The pills under the greeting say who is home, how many radiators are calling for heat, and whether anything needs a look.
Favourites are one-tap tiles: a light, a scene, a door, or simply a reading, such as the car's battery.
Below the cameras is the power flow. Dots run along each line in the direction the power is going, and faster when there is more of it.
Then today's totals, what the solar has saved in pounds, and the weather station.
The Energy page tells the whole story. Live power at the top, with self-sufficiency, solar and the battery underneath.
Each hour's solar is split by roof, and measured against a dashed mark for what the forecast promised.
This shows where every kilowatt hour since midnight came from, and where it went.
And When to run it plans the washing around the sun and the battery, and shows when the grid is at its cleanest.
Heating shows every radiator in the house at once, with a boost for the whole house at the top.
Each zone has its temperature and a setpoint you can step up or down. A cold room turns blue, a warm one amber.
Every room has its own page, built from its folder in Indigo. Lights with dimmers and colour scenes, then the television and speakers.
Below them, the motion sensors, the room's radiators, and its windows and doors.
The menu holds the rest: cameras, scenes, a timeline that replays any day, the cost of it all, alerts and Wi-Fi.
And System answers the other question: is the server itself all right? Disk, memory, load and plugins.
A device in error, or a battery running low, is named, so you know exactly what to go and fix.
It all runs from Indigo's own web server, in any browser. No app to install, no cloud account, and nothing leaving the house.
